ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of each individual UBO, manager (gérant), signatory and any beneficial owner against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), the FATF high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdiction lists, the EU common list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions and domestic Luxembourg PEP databases supported by the FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF) and the Ministry of Justice; screening must be performed at onboarding and refreshed every 24 hours to capture newly published sanctions during the engagement; any positive hit or suspicious activity must be escalated to the CRF within 24 hours; enhanced due diligence, including senior management approval, independent verification of source of funds and a complete written AML file, is mandatory for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions and complex multi-tier cross-holding structures under CSSF Regulation 12-02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) ePortal - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), pre-incorporation name verification and reservation module (https://www.lbr.lu / https://www.rcs.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory filings and corporate documents must be drafted in French, German or Luxembourgish; the company name must use the Latin script with standard diacritics; a name originating in a non-Latin script (Cyrillic, Arabic, Han, Greek or other) must be rendered in a phonetic Latin transliteration accompanied by a certified French translation; the name must be unique and clearly distinguished in the RCS against existing names, must not be misleading as to the legal form, must not be contrary to public order or bonnes mœurs and must not be identical or confusingly similar to protected corporate signs; for an SCSp, the partnership form must be apparent through the name or accepted statutory suffix (SCSp, S.C.Sp., SCS).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (requires an establishment licence and prior CSSF approval)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance / Reinsurance (requires CAA licence and ministerial approval)
Fonds d'investissement / Investment Fund / SICAV / SICAF / Fonds de placement / Collective Investment Undertaking (requires CSSF registration and prior ministerial authorization)
PFS / Professionnel du secteur financier / PSF (statutorily protected regulated professional title)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Clearing House (misleading regulated financial infrastructure terms)
État / Ministère / Commune / Municipal / Public Authority (suggests official governmental status)
Université / École / Académie / Chambre de Commerce (protected statutory titles)
Luxembourg (as a lead token requiring prior state-authority clearance when implying official endorsement)
SOPARFI / Holding 1929 (tax-legal designations subject to Administrative Registration of the company and tax bulletin compliance conditions)
Tokens contrary to public order or bonnes mœurs, including paramilitary, drug-related or offensive wording
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects or conditions a proposed name, the notary or the founder may within 15 days of the refusal decision file a written réclamation (objection) with Luxembourg Business Registers, submitting either a revised name or arguments establishing distinctiveness and compliance with Art. 4 of the Law of 19 December 2002; if the objection is dismissed, an administrative appeal may be lodged before the Tribunal Administratif (Luxembourg Administrative Court) within 3 months of notification under the Law of 7 November 1996 organizing the administrative courts; alternatively, the applicant may file a fresh de novo name-reservation request for a different available name; extension of a reserved name is not automatic and requires a new two-month reservation request before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Luxembourg law (Law of 10 August 1915, Art. 158-1) requires the SCSp to have a registered office (siège social) in the Grand Duchy; a mail-only virtual office does not satisfy the statutory standard of genuine registered seat and effective management; use of a licensed domiciliation company is permitted only where the SCSp maintains verifiable economic substance in Luxembourg (leased operational premises, locally present management, staff and complete accounting records); for an M&A advisory boutique engaged in taxable operational services, a pure virtual office is assessed by the ACD (Administration des contributions directes) as insufficient for tax residence and by AML/CFT supervisors as non-compliant for business conduct, so a professional serviced office with physical Luxembourg presence is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a domiciliation-company arrangement: 40-55% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the ACD, FIU/CRF or the Luxembourg judicial police (Police Judiciaire) within the first 24 months; for a boutique with genuine leased premises and locally located management: below 10% likelihood of an unannounced physical visit in year one; any suspicious-activity filing or unexplained capital flows materially escalate the inspection probability; the notary, the RBE administrator and CSSF-registered professionals retain desk-based AML/CFT verification powers throughout the pre-incorporation phase.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 31-1 to 31-13 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector (for regulated Professional of the Financial Sector activities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: The partnership deed (contrat de société / acte de société) filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. The SCSp is exempt from statutory legal capital requirements; the partnership deed freely fixes the agreed capital, which may be contributed in cash, in kind, or as a mere promise to contribute. No escrow account is required under Luxembourg law unless contractually or regulatorily imposed (e.g., CSSF initial capital of EUR 50,000 or equivalent professional indemnity cover for a regulated Professional of the Financial Sector).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding parties hereby form the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) and subscribe to the partnership interests set out in the signature schedule, each subscriber contributing the agreed capital to the partnership as recorded in the deed. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the partnership be fixed in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg at the address designated by the general partner and that beneficial-owner register requirements be satisfied. RESOLVED, that the general partner shall hold full management and representation powers, and that the appointment of the day-to-day manager, with sole-signature authority and the power to open bank accounts, is hereby approved, registered, and ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp Partnership Deed and Founder Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary / external legal counsel; Maison des Notaires du Luxembourg (notarial form required only for real-property or certain in-kind contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and finalize the SCSp deed covering the firm name, registered office, purpose, capital, contributions, governance powers of the general partner, decision-making rules, and winding-up provisions. Each general and limited partner (or their lawful proxy) executes the deed; foreign signatures must be legalized or apostilled. AML/KYC records for every partner and beneficial owner are collected in accordance with the Law of 12 November 2004. If the SCSp receives real estate contributions, the deed must be executed in notarial form; a private deed is valid for cash-only formations.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership deed (draft and final versions)
Passport or national ID of each partner and beneficial owner
Proof of registered-office address or letter of comfort from landlord
Duly completed powers of attorney and legalization/apostille certificates
AML/KYC source-of-funds evidence and corporate extracts for any entity shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If legalization or AML documentation is deficient or the deed conflicts with RCS form requirements, amend and re-execute the deed; if identity evidence is challenged, resubmit certified or apostilled copies and obtain notarial corrections before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: LBR / RCS Registration and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic single-submission window via the Guichet.lu / e-justice portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed SCSp deed with the RCS through the LBR single-submission portal together with the module containing details of the general partner, managers, registered office, and activity codes. After validation and payment of the statutory filing fee, the RCS issues the registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and automatically causes publication in the RESA. The central legal entity identification number is issued at the same time.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership deed and legalization/apostille records
RCS identification module forms and authorized-signatory declarations
AML/KYC beneficial-owner declarations
Receipt of state filing fee
Consent of the general partner to act as administrator of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, respond within the statutory deadline (typically 8 calendar days) by correcting the filing; if the application is refused, submit a written request for re-examination to the RCS and, as a last resort, appeal before the Luxembourg administrative courts within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Certificate, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the post-registration formalities: the AEDT registers the SCSp for VAT and corporate tax based on the RCS extract and the declared economic activity; VAT number allocation is automatic in most cases. Where persons will work in Luxembourg (manager or employees), register them with the CCSS, obtain a social security affiliation certificate, and verify expatriate social-security coordination where applicable.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract and national identification number
Declaration of economic activities and short business plan
Commercial lease or premises-occupancy evidence
Identification of any Luxembourg resident staff and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or tax registration is delayed or misclassified, lodge a corrective declaration with AEDT and request a service-level confirmation; if the CCSS contests employment status, file a position paper and, if necessary, request an administrative ruling from the social security authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Directorate of Establishment Authorizations; electronic submission through MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the business establishment permit covering independent professional activity. File the application with proof of professional honorability and financial capacity, the deed, RCS extract, and a description of the M&A advisory services. The permit confirms compliance with the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to independent professions and is a prerequisite for commencing operations.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and certified copy of the SCSp deed
Apostilled police record or certificate of good conduct
Statement of financial capacity and solvency
Detailed activity description and business plan for the M&A boutique
Professional indemnity insurance certificate, if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is queried, supplement the requested documentation within 15 calendar days; if the permit is refused, invoke the administrative-law remedies before the administrative courts within three months, or adjust the planned service perimeter to the notified regulated activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CSSF Financial Sector Licence (Professional of the Financial Sector)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) — Authorisations Unit; electronic filing via the CSSF e-file portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a complete authorization request with the CSSF for a Professional of the Financial Sector (PSF) license enabling corporate-finance M&A advisory, investment advice, and reception/transmission of orders where offered. The application must include the programme of operations, internal governance rules, AML/CFT compliance policy, fit-and-proper documentation for the general partner, manager and shareholders, initial capital or indemnity proof, and the final registered deed.
required_dossiers: Complete CSSF PSF authorization form and schedules
Detailed business plan with 3-year forecast P&L, liquidity, and risk analysis
AML/CFT policy implementing the Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF standards
Clean criminal-record extracts for each manager and responsible officer
Beneficial-owner organigram and shareholder statements
Evidence of initial capital (EUR 50,000 minimum, or equivalent indemnity cover)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to every CSSF information request within the procedurally prescribed deadlines (usually three months cumulative); if the license is refused, appeal to the Cour administrative within three months, or alternatively narrow the scope to purely unregulated corporate-finance advice and re-submit a simplified declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Office Premises Clearance, Bank Account Opening and Commencement of Business
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ville de Luxembourg Municipal Permit Service; Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); CSSF and RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure the physical premises: obtain the lease, municipal occupancy/renovation confirmation, and fire-safety certificate required by the commune. Open the operating bank account at a Luxembourg credit institution under a banking mandate naming the manager; notify the RCS, AEDT, and CSSF of the effective commencement-of-business date and the physical office address before the first consulting engagement is invoiced.
required_dossiers: RCS extract, CSSF license and deed
Lease agreement or landlord comfort letter
Fire-safety inspection certificate for the premises
Bank mandates, account-opening KYC pack and source-of-funds records
ITM employee declaration if staff are appointed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the occupancy certificate, supply a structural engineer's load-report and remedy the fire-safety findings; if the bank account opening is delayed, notify CSSF and use an interim permission to hold client funds with a recognized non-resident credit institution until a Luxembourg account is operative.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) jointly with the Ministry of the Economy — Directorate of Establishment Authorizations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Professional of the Financial Sector (PSF) authorization for M&A corporate-finance advisory services under the Law of 5 April 1993, as amended, complemented by the business establishment certificate (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — non-classified office-only activities; no Environmental Impact Assessment is required under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, and no integrated environmental permit (class 1 or 2) applies to an M&A advisory boutique occupying exclusively office premises with no industrial installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office waste segregation compliant with the Law of 9 May 2014 on waste prevention and management (separate collection of paper, packaging, glass, and WEEE per EU Directive 2012/19/EU); no process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by the activity; for any fit-out works, the building must meet the energy-performance requirements of the Règlement grand-ducal of 21 October 2017 implementing Directive 2010/31/EU.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety attestation for office occupancy issued upon favorable inspection by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) and the competent municipal fire-prevention service; structural and evacuation-load compliance per Luxembourg construction regulations; workplace-safety clearance verified by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Labour Code, including exit routes, first-aid equipment, electrical safety, ergonomic conditions, and annual staff safety training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct taxes - portal impotsdirects.public.lu; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties - portal aed.public.lu; unified electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned SCSp: (1) register the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), which automatically issues the 13-digit national identification number (NIF) used for income tax formalities; (2) file VAT registration with the AEDT (form 664) to obtain the LU + 8-digit VAT identification number; non-established taxable persons must register via a Luxembourg fiscal representative before supplying services in Luxembourg - no de minimis turnover threshold applies to non-residents, whereas residents benefit from the EUR 35,000 small-business franchise; (3) nominate a local tax agent as correspondence recipient if no permanent establishment is created.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: the SCSp has no legal personality and is fiscally transparent by default - income is taxed at partner level pro rata; entity-level corporate income tax and municipal business tax do not apply; nevertheless, the SCSp is an independent VAT taxable person and may elect into transparency or entity-level taxation as described below.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) Opt-in to full Luxembourg corporate income tax / municipal business tax liability under Article 168 of the Income Tax Law (LIR) - binding election by the partnership with partner consent, valid for five years, used to avoid hybrid mismatch outcomes and to access treaty benefits; (2) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Article 61 of the VAT Law for related Luxembourg entities; (3) ATAD/hybrid-mismatch alignment election under Articles 168ter-168septies LIR to re-characterise payments or deny double non-taxation; (4) application of the participation exemption regime (Article 166 LIR) for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutee - TVA), Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (Article 5 of the VAT Law small-business exemption) for Luxembourg-established suppliers; for non-established foreign suppliers the threshold is zero - any supply taking place in Luxembourg requires immediate VAT registration; M&A boutique advisory services to Luxembourg-established clients therefore trigger VAT registration regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API, or digital stamping mandate is in force for 2025. Mandatory e-invoicing applies for B2G supplies to the Luxembourg central government (law of 16 July 2021, operational since 2023) through the Peppol network (Peppol BIS format); B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary but substantially supported; the SCSp must be Peppol-ready for public-sector M&A mandates and should retain complete audit trails for all success-fee invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated (0%) treatment applies to: (i) export of goods dispatched or transported to a non-EU destination (Article 29 of the VAT Law); (ii) intra-Community supplies to a taxable person holding a valid EU VAT ID (Article 155 of the VAT Law); (iii) services ancillary to export transport. Cross-border M&A advisory success fees are outside Luxembourg's VAT scope under the general reverse-charge/B2B place-of-supply rule (customer establishment), and therefore neither Luxembourg VAT nor zero-rating documentation applies; if a foreign client is a private consumer in Luxembourg, the 17% standard rate applies. The SCSp must maintain partner-level allocation evidence because the transparency regime shifts VAT deduction and recovery to partners.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document) processed in the electronic export control system and exit confirmation from the EU customs office
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical removal from the EU
Commercial invoice and signed engagement/success-fee agreement
SWIFT inward remittance certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of consideration
Customer's valid EU VAT identification number (for intra-Community supplies to taxable persons)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess VAT for five years (ten years in case of fraud). Unsubstantiated zero-rating or intra-Community claims trigger recovery of underpaid VAT, default interest at 0.8% per month, and administrative fines up to EUR 12,500 per infringement under Article 64 of the VAT Law; criminal tax fraud (Article 62) carries imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fines up to EUR 25,000. For the SCSp, input VAT clawbacks must be borne by the partners per profit-sharing ratios, and fraudulent export documentation can void the entire engagement fee deduction. Luxembourg has no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is a documentary best practice used by AEDT examiners for inward remittance evidence and by the banking AML framework, but prolonged non-repatriation may trigger transfer-pricing or treaty-abuse review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) retains supervisory competence for AML/CFT and banking conduct. Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange control agency; capital-movement surveillance derives from the Law of 27 December 1990 on the liberalisation of capital movements and the ECB Statistical Regulation (EU) 2013/2707, with BCL acting as the national compiler of Balance of Payments (BoP) statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility for euro-zone and non-EEA transfers, in line with Articles 63–65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The euro is freely convertible; there are no profit-remittance restrictions, no foreign-exchange licensing, and no requirement to channel transfers through authorised dealers. A Luxembourg SCSp is tax-transparent (non-fiscale) for income tax purposes, so distributions of success-fee profits to non-resident Limited Partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax unless the partner is in a non-cooperative jurisdiction blacklisted by the EU. Practical impediments arise only from AML transparency: banks require the RBE beneficial-owner register, source-of-funds evidence, and a legal opinion before wiring fees to third parties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender or conversion ratio for export proceeds, no repatriation deadline, and no obligation to convert foreign-currency service fees (including M&A success fees under ISIC 7020) into euro. The sole administrative duty is the BCL balance-of-payments statistical return for individual transactions equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 per counterparty per calendar quarter, reported via the BCL's BDP (Balance of Payments) web interface using the ECB BoP classification for services income. Funds may be retained in USD, GBP, CHF, or any other account currency indefinitely.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — approved only for operational treasury overflow and client-fee receipt, never for the capital-escrow layer. A Luxembourg SCSp may legally open a payment account with a CSSF-licensed Electronic Money Institution (Law of 10 August 2018) or with a passported EU/EEA EMI under the PSD2 regime (Law of 10 November 2009). Offshore digital EMIs from third countries (e.g., non-EEA jurisdictions) cannot provide payment accounts in Luxembourg without a CSSF-authorised branch; using one would constitute the unauthorised carrying-out of payment services under Article 30 of the Law of 10 November 2009 and a breach of CSSF Circular 12/552 on the provision of payment services. Even a passported EMI will be treated by tier-1 banks as an 'unregulated intermediary' for the purposes of source-of-funds verification, so the SCSp must maintain a primary euro liquidity buffer at a fully licensed credit institution with a traditional SWIFT BIC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote-only opening is not accepted for an SCSp. In practice, the General Partner's authorised representative (manager or director) must attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank's Luxembourg office or, in a strictly limited alternative, at the Luxembourg embassy/consulate with a certified true signature followed by a notarised countersignature. Under CSSF Regulation No 18-04 and FATF Recommendation 10, a physical presence mandate is justified by the SCSp's lack of legal personality. Where the GP is itself a corporate entity, the bank requires its own identification of the GP's managers and UBOs, and a separate interview for the designated signatories of the account; an intermediary Trust and Company Service Provider (TCSP) may attend jointly but cannot replace the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp without legal personality, combined with non-resident Limited Partners holding indirect economic control through a cascade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement (contrat de société) filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); extract of the RBE beneficial-ownership register filed within one month of account opening; a Luxembourg notarial legal opinion confirming the SCSp's separate patrimoine d'affectation and the GP's power of representation; a full ownership chain from each LP to the ultimate natural persons; certified KYC files (passport, proof of address, source-of-funds declaration) for every UBO; and, if any LP is a regulated fund, its latest AIFM/RIF documentation or regulatory status certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border M&A advisory activity generating high-value success fees from clients resident in non-EEA, higher-risk jurisdictions or sanction-prone sectors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement letter with defined mandate, success-fee waterfall, and fee-schedule formula; the underlying transaction documents (SPA, share transfer agreement, closing certificate) proving a real commercial event; a Luxembourg economic-substance record (substantive office, employment contracts of local managers/analysts, substance return); an EU-targeted sanctions screening report against the CSSF financial-sanctions list; and a client-source evaluation report evidencing that no funds originated from politically exposed persons connected to state procurement in a high-risk country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital inflows from Limited Partners resident in blacklisted or non-Cooperative jurisdictions (EU Annex II) or from shell entities with opaque ultimate ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution notices matching the partnership agreement's drawdown schedule; LP bank statements evidencing the onward transfer from a regulated account; W-8BEN-E / CRS self-certification forms for each LP; a legal opinion from Luxembourg tax counsel confirming the transaction falls outside the Luxembourg anti-abuse provisions (Law of 23 December 2005, Grand-Ducal Decree of 31 July 2020 on substance); and a rejected-transaction protocol committing the SCSp to decline contributions from jurisdictions that fail the FATF beneficial-ownership transparency standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Temporary 'closing-spike' flow pattern of a six- or seven-figure success-fee credit grossly exceeding the advisory boutique's historical run-rate, creating a transaction-monitoring alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Boutique financial statements and 12-month revenue ledger; the engagement letter's success-fee clause cross-referenced to the exact closing date; the notary's escrow account settlement statement; a final fee invoice with detailed reference to the stage-gate milestones achieved; and an explanation letter from the GP confirming that the fee formula is non-discretionary and capped by the underlying transaction agreement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident Limited Partners are cleared via SWIFT MT103 (for non-EEA) or SEPA Credit Transfer (for EEA/EU partners) to the SCSp's segregated account at a BCL-regulated bank. The required payment reference block must read: 'LU SCSp [name] – Capital Contribution – [LP legal name] – [qtr/year] – [contribution notice ID]'. The bank verifies the remitter against the RBE register and applies an early-warning AML block on any discrepancy. For BCL statistical compliance, the contribution is reported in the quarterly BDP return under the ECB BoP financial-account item 'Direct investment – Equity capital – inward' (code 51011 in the Eurostat v2 classification), regardless of whether the partnership is treated as quasi-transparent for accounting purposes. A formal capital-call notice (Fonds d'appel) signed by the GP must be pre-delivered to the bank, and the final credit must not exceed the aggregate commitments registered in the partnership agreement, otherwise the surplus is redeemed pending clarification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade settlements is SWIFT MT103 (or MT202COV for cover payments through a EUR/USD correspondent chain) for non-EEA suppliers and SEPA Instant/SEPA CT for EEA counterparties. For high-value acquisition escrows, a commercial documentary Letter of Credit may be opened under UCP 600, or a demand guarantee under URDG 758, with the bank's trade-finance desk. Success-fee disbursements from the SCSp to the advisory boutique (ASBL/EURL, if distinct) are executed as MT103 with the purpose code 'General Services – Professional and consulting fees' and must be supported by a fee invoice and the engagement letter; the beneficiary's account must hold the same beneficial ownership or the transaction is escalated to a dual-control approval by the bank's transaction-monitoring unit. USD-denominated wires route via BGL BNP Paribas' New York clearing (Fedwire/CHIPS) or via CITI/BONY correspondent accounts at Société Générale Bank & Trust, with a per-wire correspondent cost of EUR 6–25 and a potential FX compression fee if a currency conversion is embedded.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) to fix the euro value of hard-currency success fees and escrow balances, transacted under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a bank holding a Luxembourg credit-institution licence.

FX swaps (rollover of a forward position through simultaneous spot-thus-forward transaction) for the conversion of non-euro capital contributions into EUR and the temporary equalisation of reserve currencies.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted-currency markets (e.g., INR, IDR, PHP) permitted only where the underlying M&A client operates in a regulated-currency jurisdiction and the SCSp can demonstrate a genuine hedging need; speculative NDF exposure is prohibited under CSSF Circular 19/707 and the GP's investment-policy statement.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (EUR/USD floating-to-floating) limited to the duration of the underlying acquisition financing and with a notional capped at the expected fee pool, requiring a board resolution of the GP and pre-approval by the bank's credit-risk committee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership Information (RBE annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days after each anniversary of the RBE registration date; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 1 month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 1,250, public notice of the penalty, suspension of partner rights, and, if the entity also fails to comply with RCS update duties, administrative strike-off from the trade register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS Event-Driven Updating Declaration (annual maintenance review of register particulars)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days after any change to the general partner, registered office, partnership agreement, or other registered particulars; no separate annual renewal return is required in Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines under Article 142 of the RCS Law and liability for damages; continued failure to update the RCS can lead to removal from the register, which triggers winding-up and loss of the RCS-registered entity status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Tax Declaration on a Fiscally Transparent Basis (SCSp pass-through declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the close of the tax year; electronically filed returns are treated as timely until 31 December of that filing year under regular ACD practice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 5,000 per return, default interest at 0.6% per month on any assessed tax, and criminal sanctions where intent to evade is established

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. An SCSp lacks legal personality and is not subject to the Luxembourg annual accounts and audit regime for commercial companies under the Law of 19 December 2002. Mandatory independent audits arise only if the SCSp is contractually required by the partnership agreement or if it is involved in a CSSF-supervised regulated activity (e.g., alternative investment fund) where specific investor protection rules apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework is imposed on an SCSp as such. Where accounts are prepared voluntarily or for tax reporting, Luxembourg GAAP under the revised Law of 19 December 2002 is commonly applied; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used where the SCSp forms part of a consolidated group or by election under applicable law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must confirm its beneficial ownership data with the RBE every year within 15 calendar days of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration. The confirmation is performed online through the LBR portal by the registered filer (usually the domiciliation agent). Any change in the identity or percentage interest of direct or indirect beneficial owners must be filed within 1 month of the change. The relevant UBO threshold is an interest of 25% plus one share or equivalent in the partnership interests, control rights, or economic rights.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: No statutory on-site register is required for an SCSp because the entity has no legal personality; the RCS and RBE electronic registers serve as the statutory records.
Optional best-practice records: partnership ledger, signed partner resolutions and written consents, and an archive of the partnership agreement and its amendments.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,200 - 7,500 per year for registered office and corporate secretarial services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for a non-regulated SCSp; if voluntarily audited or required by investor agreements, USD 6,000 - 18,000 per annual audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17%, solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax 6.75% for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent; partners are taxed at their own rates. Luxembourg offers an IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income) and a participation exemption for dividends and capital gains (100% exemption if holding ≥10% or acquisition cost ≥€6 million, and subject to certain conditions). Losses can be carried forward indefinitely.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via the Luxembourg eCDF (Electronic Tax Filing) portal; for SCSp, the partnership files an annual information return (Form 500) to report income allocation to partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end, unless an extension is granted (typically up to 6 months).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp (name, address, RCS number, tax ID).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg tax ID and registered office address; non-resident partners must be identified with their foreign tax IDs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of taxable income (or loss) for the fiscal year, including all income from M&A advisory services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, report their share of income as allocated in the partnership agreement; ensure compliance with Luxembourg tax rules on foreign partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and allowances (e.g., operating expenses, depreciation, interest, and any IP box deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim deductions only if they are attributable to Luxembourg-source income; maintain proper documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayments (e.g., withholding tax credits, advance payments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim foreign tax credits if applicable under a tax treaty; attach Form 500 and supporting TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of related-party transactions (transfer pricing) and any cross-border payments (royalties, interest, dividends).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must disclose any transactions with related parties and ensure arm's length pricing; attach TP documentation if thresholds are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: €250 to €2,500 per month of delay, plus interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax. For intentional non-filing, penalties can reach 10% of the tax due, and criminal sanctions may apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the parent holds ≥10% for at least 12 months; also 0% under Luxembourg participation exemption for qualifying holdings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the partner's jurisdiction and apply for reduced withholding tax via the Luxembourg tax administration (AED) before the distribution. The application must include the DTA article, proof of ownership, and a declaration of beneficial ownership. Approval is typically granted within 3 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10% (reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive if the beneficial owner is an EU company holding ≥25% for at least 24 months; treaty rates may apply). Interest: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under the same directive; treaty rates often 0-10%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group revenue (for Master File) and EUR 1 million related-party transactions (for Local File) trigger mandatory TP documentation. For SCSp, the partnership must prepare a Local File if its related-party transactions exceed EUR 1 million, and a Master File if the group revenue exceeds EUR 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: SCSp is not subject to Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as it is a partnership, but it must demonstrate sufficient economic substance (e.g., office, staff, decision-making) to avoid being classified as a shell company under Luxembourg anti-abuse rules and to maintain treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or failure to file tax returns for the SCSp or its partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax, plus interest at 0.6% per month. Criminal prosecution may result in fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no physical presence, no employees, no real business activity, and is used solely to channel funds or avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of the entity as taxable, and imposition of a 10% penalty on the tax due. The entity may be struck off the register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the company's tax liabilities if they fail to ensure substance; civil penalties and potential criminal charges for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct adequate customer due diligence, report suspicious transactions, or maintain records for M&A advisory fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €5 million or 10% of annual turnover for legal entities; suspension of license; criminal prosecution for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal fines up to €1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years for willful AML violations; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length pricing in cross-border transactions with related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 10% of the adjustment, and interest. In severe cases, criminal penalties for tax evasion may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they approved the non-compliant pricing; civil restitution and potential criminal charges.
